haiku-low.q1: A pending login: no session is created. The server stores a pending login and sets the p2f cookie, and the user must still enter a second factor.
haiku-low.q2: Only after setup is confirmed with a valid app code. Until then, sign-in keeps checking the confirmed secret, and unconfirmed secrets are never used.
haiku-low.q3: The recovery code is marked used, an email is queued saying a code was used and how many remain, and the user is signed in. Sign-in does not depend on the email.
haiku-low.q4: The 5th wrong entry or the 5-minute limit deletes the pending login. The user must start again from the password step.
haiku-low.q5: On first setup confirmation, all other sessions are signed out and the current session stays. Replacement does not sign out other sessions; the brief leaves this open.
haiku-low.q6: No. Once a time step is accepted, that step and earlier steps are refused for that user. Codes from the current, previous or next 30-second step are accepted.
haiku-low.q7: The secret is marked confirmed, its time step is recorded, old recovery codes are replaced by 10 new ones, and on first setup other sessions are signed out. Partial failure: NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: Stored in the pending_logins table, keyed by a hash of the random token in the browser's p2f cookie. Removed on success, on the 5th wrong entry, or after 5 minutes.
haiku-low.q9: Secret, confirmed flag and last accepted time step are in user_totp; recovery code hashes and used flags are in recovery_codes. 2FA is on when a confirmed secret exists.
haiku-low.q10: The old confirmed secret keeps protecting sign-in until the new one is confirmed. If abandoned, the old secret keeps working and the unconfirmed new secret is inert.
haiku-low.q11: How the second step distinguishes the two is NOT STATED. Wrong recovery codes count: a used or unmatched recovery code is a wrong entry toward the limit of 5.
haiku-low.q12: Not designed. No transition is drawn, and the only route is an unused recovery code. Whether support may reset 2FA, and how identity is checked, is open.

sonnet.q1: A pending login only: a pending_logins row and the p2f cookie. No session is created, so the user is not signed in.
sonnet.q2: Once the secret is confirmed (valid app code entered). 2FA is on only when a confirmed secret exists; an unconfirmed secret is never used for sign-in.
sonnet.q3: The code is marked used, an email is queued saying a code was used and how many remain, and the user is signed in (pending login deleted). Sign-in does not depend on the email; it is queued and retried in the background.
sonnet.q4: The 5th wrong entry or 5 minutes elapsing. The pending login is deleted and the user goes back to the password step and must start over.
sonnet.q5: On first setup confirmation, all other sessions of that user are signed out; the current session stays.
sonnet.q6: No. After a code from a time step is accepted, that step and all earlier ones are refused. Tolerance is one 30-second step before or after the current one (about +/-30 seconds).
sonnet.q7: Secret marked confirmed (replacement: secret replaced), time step of that code recorded, old recovery codes deleted and 10 new ones created (shown once); first setup also signs out other sessions. What happens if the update fails partway: NOT STATED (the document says the three things are done 'together' but gives no failure behavior; a wrong/used code is rejected and state stays unchanged).
sonnet.q8: In the pending_logins table (user, hash of token, expiry 5 minutes after password check, wrong-entry count). The browser holds the p2f cookie with a random token; only its hash is stored. It is removed on successful sign-in, on the 5th wrong entry, or on expiry (5 minutes).
sonnet.q9: Secret (sealed with seal(), key in KMS), confirmed flag, and last accepted time step are all in the user_totp row (one per user). Recovery codes are in recovery_codes (hashed, with used flag, up to 10 per user). 2FA is on only when a confirmed secret exists.
sonnet.q10: The old confirmed secret keeps working for sign-in, since the new secret is saved unconfirmed. If abandoned, the unconfirmed secret is inert: never used for sign-in and overwritten by the next setup or replacement; the old authenticator stays in effect.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED how the server distinguishes the two input types. Wrong entries: a used or unmatched recovery code counts as a wrong entry in the pending login (toward the limit of 5).
sonnet.q12: No designed path. Product must still decide whether support can reset 2FA and how identity would be verified. The only route to a new authenticator is signing in with an unused recovery code.
